operations.title: Exact integral and modular deck-norm locus audit
operations.method: For cyclic regular lattices of kernel orders 2 through 12, verify N_K^2=|K|N_K, normalized projectors at good primes, and nonzero square-zero norms at primes dividing |K|.

operations.title: The deck norm derives a conditional bad-prime locus supported on the kernel order
operations.body: Given an independently integral deck lattice, e_K=N_K/|K| is an idempotent over Z[1/|K|]. Its integral normalization obstruction is supported on V(|K|); modulo each p dividing |K|, the nonzero regular norm is square-zero. This derives an arithmetic support locus from deck multiplicity, but does not derive Spec Z or primes from the bare Carrier and supplies no physical relative-chain pushforward.

operations.outcome: pass: 649 integral norm-quadratic checks, 2965 good-prime projector checks, and 929 bad-prime nonzero square-zero checks

evidence.paraphrase: Exact matrix enumeration identifies precisely the prime divisors of each kernel order as the normalization-degeneration locus.

operations.title: Grothendieck derives the conditional bad-prime support of the deck norm
operations.body: With the physical branch-chain lift still absent, I attacked the strongest algebraic arithmetic consequence of the paired norm. On an independently integral deck lattice, e_K=N_K/|K| is an idempotent over Z[1/|K|]; the obstruction is supported on V(|K|). Modulo every p dividing |K|, N_K remains nonzero on the regular module but satisfies N_K^2=0. Exact cyclic checks for |K|=2..12 give 649 integral quadratic checks, 2965 good-prime projector checks, and 929 bad-prime square-zero checks. Thus the five-site 2-group branch tower canonically has bad locus V(2). Scope is strict: this is arithmetic derived from an already integral coefficient lattice and deck multiplicity, not a derivation of Spec Z/primes from the bare Carrier, not Frobenius or Euler product data, and not physical q_* admission.
